answer: Like a canyon that only lets a slow river through, an agent economy can impose an entry queue with an aging period: a new identity may register at once, but it cannot earn until it has waited weeks and completed small verified jobs. A zephyr of fresh Sybils cannot flood the market, because each fake must sit idle on a shale ledge of time before it pays off. Attackers face weeks of delay per identity, while honest newcomers simply wait once and keep working.
